annotationMethod: Derived from benchmarks/annotations/merit-real-venue.json by benchmarks/robustness/make-variants.mjs. The image is the real Golden Plan with the "rotate-2" transform applied (a page scanned slightly askew); every object and region was put through the same geometric map the pixels were, so the truth is exact rather than reused. THIS IS NOT A SECOND REAL VENUE PLAN — it is the same drawing rendered differently, and any accuracy it shows says nothing about a venue this system has not seen.

confidence.tables: high — every table is a solid tan component with a clean size band
confidence.chairsOrange: high — separate saturated components, individually visible
confidence.chairsPale: medium — recovered by angular clustering rather than as separate components, so the box is the crescent's extent in the annulus and may clip where it overlaps the table Corrected 2026-10-18: around t038 two clusters (c090, c094) were merged boxes 91 px wide centred inside the table, standing for three chairs, and around t040 one chair was split into two half-boxes (c101, c107). c090, c094 and a new c114 now hold t038's right, lower-right and lower chairs as measured by benchmarks/annotate/round-table-chairs.py; c101 is removed. The count stays 113 (24 pale).
confidence.banquettes: high for position, none for seat count
confidence.architecture: partial — see regions; columns are NOT annotated, see capacity.note

capacity.annotatedChairsNote: 113 individually located chairs: 79 orange-armchair, 10 orange-bistro-chair, 24 pale-outlined-chair. This supersedes the earlier figure of 105, which was a count from zoomed crops with no positions and did not separate the bistro chairs from the armchairs. The drawing's own printed total is 124 pax, and the three banquettes have no drawn seat divisions, so the remaining difference is exactly the banquette capacity the drawing does not state.

unverified.reason: Three long banquettes in the top-right cluster. The drawing does not divide them into seat positions, so their capacity cannot be read off it. The gap between 105 counted chairs and the drawing's stated 124 is the size of this unknown; a capacity auditor should surface these three objects as the unresolved region rather than silently balancing the number.
